entries.claim: A read-only desk review on 2026-10-30 identified CVE-2023-28205 as the only candidate in the reviewed set that combines a public WebKit proof of concept, no JavaScript JIT requirement, and a reachable structured-clone path. The public MIT-licensed PoC targets WebKit-613.1.17.1 and triggers a use-after-free by sending a Map/Date object graph through postMessage. The Switch applet executes local JavaScript and is feature-bracketed to Safari 15.4-15.6, but at the time of the review the PoC had not been run on the console and the exact patch level was unknown; see E-113 for the later exploratory run.
entries.scope: Read-only source review on 2026-10-30. No console interaction, no PoC execution, and no exploit attempt. The review covers public advisories, the WebKit fix commit, and the public PoC.
entries.evidence: The review compared the applet's fingerprint (E-058, E-061, E-063) with public WebKit advisories and PoCs. CVE-2023-28205 is a JavaScriptCore SerializedScriptValue/CloneDeserializer use-after-free fixed by WebKit commit c9880de (MarkedVector); the public PoC uses postMessage with Map/Date objects and targets WebKit-613.1.17.1. JIT-dependent candidates (CVE-2022-42856, CVE-2023-37450, CVE-2023-41993, CVE-2024-23222, CVE-2024-44308) were excluded because the applet shows no JIT warm-up. CVE-2022-32912 was excluded because the applet has no WebGL. CVE-2023-32409 and CVE-2025-24201 were excluded as sandbox escapes that are not first-stage primitives. CVE-2024-44309 is an XSS/cookie issue. CVE-2024-27834 and CVE-2025-31201 are PAC bypasses and Switch 1 has no PAC. CVE-2025-31200 is a CoreAudio APAC decoder bug, not WebKit, and the codec is not expected on the Switch. CVE-2022-32893 remains a secondary candidate but has no public PoC in the reviewed sources. CVE-2023-4863 was already tested inconclusively in D7.
entries.limitations: The review is a desk exercise. The public PoC's crash analysis is from a PlayStation WebKit process, not the Switch. The Switch build may include a Nintendo backport of the MarkedVector fix. A browser crash would be applet-level only and would not reach Atmosphère without a separate kernel/boot-stage chain. No console page was loaded and no exploit content was served during this review; see E-113 for the later exploratory run.

No PoC was served, no crash was induced, and the exact WebKit patch level remains unknown. The full JSONL log is local-only because it contains request headers and console network identifiers. A browser compromise would be applet-level only.

entries.claim: The pinned public CVE-2023-28205 PoC was served to the Switch applet on 2026-10-31 in an exploratory four-load run. The module graph loaded in every load, the page logged only Attempt lines, and no Stage 1 trigger, alert, crash, reboot, or hang occurred. The run deviated from the approved single-page protocol, so it is not a clean negative.
entries.scope: D2 W2 exploratory run on 2026-10-31. Four page loads in crash, probe=1, and probe=2 modes over 227 s on the owner's home Wi-Fi, with the console's primary DNS temporarily set to the Mac at 192.168.178.167. The runner served the unmodified MIT-licensed PoC from commit 57126d03eeceb2e46b39adbe1fad2abf08ed33e3 (index.html SHA-256 3d9074f1c72bbff804ab84218124193b71a95c0666a9fbe0f2742c78028cc4a4, poc.js SHA-256 873fe43af25961b312ff3d24c20c15a5475a51ac359cdb572dcb150f11137be4). The owner approved the PoC's bounded localStorage log.
entries.evidence: The console at 192.168.178.136 made 79 DNS queries for ctest.cdn.nintendo.net and 45 HTTP GET requests in a 227 s session (16:35:49Z-16:39:36Z). The log records four page loads: /portal?autorun=1 at 17:36:02 local (crash default, 16 s), /portal?autorun=1&mode=crash at 17:36:18 (43 s), /portal?autorun=1&mode=probe&probe=1 at 17:37:01 (44 s), and /portal?autorun=1&mode=probe&probe=2 at 17:37:45 (58 s). Each load fetched /poc.js and /module/{utils,constants,int64,mem,rw,offset}.mjs with HTTP 200 and text/javascript. There were no POST requests. The owner reports that the page stayed, no alert or crash occurred, the Load logs view showed only Attempt lines, and the console returned to normal. The owner reverted DNS to Automatic.
entries.limitations: Protocol deviation: four page loads in four modes instead of one bounded page load, with each mode reloaded after 16-58 s. The highest Attempt count was not recorded, and the localStorage log was not exported, so the PoC may not have run long enough to reach Stage 1. No crash dump or fault address was produced. This is not a clean negative for CVE-2023-28205 and does not show the build is patched. A browser compromise would be applet-level only.

entries.claim: The public ns2jb package contains only a Switch 2 code path: the repository has only engine/switch2, run.cjs hardcodes platform 2 and target switch2, and bootstrap.bas validates Switch 2 offsets.
entries.scope: Read-only inspection of the public ns2jb repository on 2026-10-31. No code was executed and no console was touched.
entries.evidence: run.cjs builds its result object with platform: 2 and target: 'switch2', copies engine/shared and engine/switch2 into the run folder, and spawns switch2/pipeline.cjs. The repository tree has engine/switch2 but no engine/switch1. bootstrap.bas is labelled 'Switch 2 / SmileBASIC 4.4.9' and checks Switch 2-specific values such as &H9DB49C, &H5872F0, and &H12F614. The README states 'Switch 2 only'.
entries.limitations: This shows the package is not a Switch 1 port; it does not show whether the underlying fs bug exists on Switch 1. A port would need different offsets, heap grooming, and a payload, and none has been published.

entries.claim: The macOS wrapper and the maintained ns2jb forks add convenience and demo support but remain Switch 2-only and still require SmileBASIC; none adds a Switch 1 path or a free entry point.
entries.scope: Read-only review of mac2jb and the kurumuz and BermTheSequel forks on 2026-10-31.
entries.evidence: mac2jb describes itself as 'an all-in-one ns2 jailbreaking tool for Mac' and requires a Switch 2 on 23.0.1 with SmileBASIC full 4.4.9 or demo 4.4.6, Ethernet on the console, and an unsigned kernel extension with SIP disabled. The kurumuz fork says it is 'Switch 2 only', requires Ethernet on both devices, and estimates at best a 20% success rate; it adds demo support and a system-code dump. The BermTheSequel fork adds demo 4.4.6 support and Windows/Linux hosts and is still a Switch 2 FS demo.

The macOS wrapper requires an Apple Silicon Mac, Switch Ethernet, and disabling SIP to load an unsigned kernel extension, which this project does not authorize; this MacBook also has no Ethernet port or USB-C Ethernet adapter.

entries.claim: A WebKit-based ns2jb port is claimed for the Switch 2, but no public release, write-up, or Switch 1 WebKit chain was found as of 2026-10-31.
entries.scope: Public-source review on 2026-10-31.
entries.evidence: ONE Jailbreak reports a Discord claim that the fs payload works through Switch 2 WebKit on the author's console and that testers were wanted for firmware before 23.0.1. The article states that no public download or full write-up had been posted. The original write-up lists the WebKit port as future work.
entries.limitations: The port's existence and capability are author-reported and not independently reproduced. It is described only for Switch 2; the Switch 1 browser is a different, older NetFront/WebKit build, so the claim does not transfer.

entries.claim: The ns2jb author says the SmileBASIC trigger and ROP stage were developed on a Switch 1, and that the exploit was tested on Switch 1, but no Switch 1 package, offsets, payload, or firmware are published.
entries.scope: Author-reported development and test history in the public write-up; not independently reproduced.
entries.evidence: The write-up says: 'This was a Switch 1 game, so the SmileBASIC agent could work on the exploit on my Switch 1, while the WebKit agent worked on the Switch 2. After some time, it got ROP.' It later says: 'The exploit has also been tested on the Switch 1, but I haven't gotten around to packaging it yet. It wouldn't provide the capabilities of a modchip, but it wouldn't require any external hardware.' The first statement confirms SmileBASIC-triggered ROP on a Switch 1. The second claims the exploit was tested there but does not state the model, firmware, or how far the chain went.
entries.limitations: Author-reported only. No Switch 1 bootstrap, fs offsets, hashes, payload, or package is public. The Switch 1 model and firmware are unstated, so applicability to 23.0.1 is unknown. A Switch 1 test does not show the fs bug is present in the 23.0.1 build.

entries.claim: The owner's local Switch 1 23.0.1 NCA dump does not contain an NCA with title ID 0100000000000000 (fs), and every system program NCA in the 01000000000000xx range is key generation 0x17, which the supplied keys cannot decrypt.
entries.scope: Read-only parse of all 238 NCA headers in Firmware/Firmware.23.0.1 on 2026-10-31. No console interaction and no key material recorded.
entries.evidence: All 238 files parse as NCA3 after AES-XTS header decryption with the local header key. Title IDs were read at 0x210 and key generation at 0x220. No row has title ID 0100000000000000. The system program rows present in the 01000000000000xx range, including ldn at 0100000000000018, are all key generation 0x17. The key file stops at key_area_key_application_14 (20.0.0), so generation 0x17 content cannot be decrypted.
entries.limitations: This shows the fs NCA is absent from this dump and that generation 0x17 content is not decryptable with the supplied keys. It does not show that fs is absent from the console or that the Switch 1 fs lacks the path-normalization bug. The dump is owner-supplied and folder-named 23.0.1; its version was not independently verified.

entries.claim: The benign H-013 image displayed the owner's real Exif control screenshot with no error, and the Album did not display the AA\<CJK> sibling directory; the Album does not traverse non-date directories under NINTENDO/ALBUM.
entries.scope: Owner observation, one console, 2026-10-31. Benign image only; the crafted image was not written.
entries.evidence: The corrected benign image contained the real Exif screenshot at NINTENDO/ALBUM/2026/10/27/2026102700452400-57B4628D2267231D57E0FC1078C0596D.jpg and a long AA\<CJK> sibling directory under NINTENDO/ALBUM. The Album displayed the control image with no error or crash and did not display the AA\<CJK> directory. The control confirms the card path, filename, and Exif requirements.

entries.claim: The captive-portal applet exposes no HTML download attribute, no save/open/directory picker, and no navigator.storage or caches API. It does expose <input type=file>, indexedDB, and localStorage.
entries.scope: One capability page load on 2026-10-31 through the local captive portal; no download click, no crafted filename, no SD-card write.
entries.evidence: The download_probe event reported anchorDownload=false, anchorDownloadType=undefined, showSaveFilePicker/showOpenFilePicker/showDirectoryPicker=undefined, storage=undefined, storageEstimate=false, storageGetDirectory=false, caches=undefined, serviceWorker=false. It reported inputFile=true, inputFiles=true, inputWebkitDirectory=false, inputDirectory=false, blob/createObjectURL/FileReader/fetch/xhr present, indexedDB/localStorage/sessionStorage present. UA: Mozilla/5.0 (Nintendo Switch; WifiWebAuthApplet) AppleWebKit/613.0 (KHTML, like Gecko) NF/6.0.3.31.11 NintendoBrowser/5.1.0.55481. No benign_download_clicked event was logged.
entries.limitations: Feature presence is not proof that the file picker opens or that the applet passes a selected file's full path to fs. The page JS would see a File object, not the full path. This does not test a crafted path or the fs bug.

entries.claim: The captive-portal applet renders a file input but pressing Browse reports 'The file selection is not supported'; file selection is unavailable.
entries.scope: Owner observation, one console, 2026-10-31. File-picker probe page via the local portal; no file was selected and no contents were read.
entries.evidence: The file-picker page displayed 'ready; choose a file'. Pressing Browse produced the applet message 'The file selection is not supported'. No file_picker event was logged. The H-013 real-control SD card was inserted.
entries.limitations: One applet and one page. The message is an applet-level restriction; it does not prove that another applet or a full browser lacks file selection.

entries.claim: Seedsow Lullaby (Artemis engine) has a save-based Lua 5.1 primitive: a modified save runs arbitrary Lua inside the game on Switch 1 and Switch 2. The free demo works. The Lua environment has save and game: VFS access, but no shell, no sd:, and /../ traversal is normalized away.
entries.scope: Public repository and hardware results, 2026-10-31; no OLED 23.0.1 test.
entries.evidence: The Seedsow Lua Editor runs Lua inside Seedsow Lullaby on Switch 1 and Switch 2; the tested reference is US demo 1.0.0. ns2-savekit reports Lua 5.1 with io, os, debug, package, loadstring, and dofile; os.execute returns 0, io.popen is unsupported, sd: is absent, and save:/../saveg.dat is normalized away. The editor save is installed with JKSV on a hacked Switch 1 and moved with Nintendo's official save transfer.
entries.limitations: This is game-level Lua, not fs-level. The fs sysmodule exploit is untested through this path and the Artemis/FS bootstrap is not public. The save is version-specific; the OLED 23.0.1 route has not been tested. The seed console and current-firmware transfer are required.

entries.claim: The Seedsow installation route requires a hacked Switch 1 seed console that can run homebrew and complete Nintendo's official save transfer, with both consoles on current firmware. The owner's only hacked Switch 1 is on 22.0.0, the 23.0.1 source console is gone, and the modded 22.0.0 console is off-limits by prior decision.
entries.scope: Installation requirements plus owner hardware inventory, 2026-10-31.
entries.evidence: The editor README says to start with a modded/hacked Switch 1 that can run homebrew and can complete Nintendo's online save transfer; both consoles need to be current for the official transfer. The owner has the unmodded 23.0.1 OLED and a modded 22.0.0 Switch 1; the 23.0.1 source console is no longer available. The 22.0.0 console has been left untouched by prior decision.

entries.claim: Nintendo's official save transfer requires the latest system version on the consoles. The owner's seed console is on 22.0.0 and the OLED is on 23.0.1, so the transfer is blocked as-is without updating the seed.
entries.scope: Official Nintendo support plus owner hardware inventory, 2026-10-31.
entries.evidence: Nintendo's support page says: 'You must update to the latest system version before carrying out a transfer.' The Seedsow Lua Editor guide also says both consoles need to be current for the official transfer. The owner's only hacked Switch 1 is on 22.0.0; the OLED is on 23.0.1; the 23.0.1 source console is gone.
entries.limitations: The support page is generic and the transfer tool might behave differently for a specific game/version. A harmless normal-save transfer test could confirm it, but that requires using the modded seed console and the OLED.

entries.claim: The console SD card's NCA containers are NAX0-encrypted; the global NCA header key does not decrypt them. Nintendo/Contents/private is a 16-byte SD-seed identifier, not the seed; the actual seed is in the console's internal system save 8000000000000043, which is not on the card. Only the FAT tree is readable.
entries.scope: Read-only inventory of the SD card inserted 2026-10-31. No content extraction and no key output.
entries.evidence: The card is a 31.9 GB FAT32 volume with Nintendo/Album (empty), Nintendo/Contents/registered (four NCA containers: 19,968; 389,632; 165,376; 1,748,484,096 bytes), and Nintendo/save (8000000000000000, 1,916,928 bytes; 8000000000000124, 21,413,888 bytes). The NCA data files are <hash>.nca/00 and do not decrypt to NCA3 with the global header key; their first bytes are high-entropy. Nintendo/Contents/private is 16 bytes; the SD-seed system save 8000000000000043 is absent. The save files are high-entropy. Most prod.keys are global (master_key, titlekek, key_area_key_application, header_key, and sd_card_nca_key_source are reusable across consoles), but the NAX0 key derivation also requires the per-console sd_seed, and save data uses per-console save keys. The local sd_seed belongs to the source console, not the OLED.
entries.limitations: If the card came from the lost 23.0.1 source console, its sd_seed in the local prod.keys might decrypt the NAX0 headers; this was not tested. If the card is the OLED's, the seed is internal and unavailable without CFW. No title IDs or key generations are claimed.

entries.claim: As of 2026-11-01 Gezine's Switch 1/2 userland exploit has no public release, repository, technical write-up, or reproduction. Gezine's public GitHub contains no Switch exploit project, and the October physical-cartridge and untethered-jailbreak claims are Switch 2-specific and unreleased.
entries.scope: Public release status checked on 2026-11-01 against Gezine's GitHub API listing and three news sources.
entries.evidence: The GitHub API lists 12 public repositories, most recently updated 2026-11-01; all are PS4/PS5 or general tooling (Y2JB, BD-JB5, Luac0re, elfldr, ftpsrv, remote_lua_loader, sdk, kexp). ArtemisLuaLoader, the closest Switch-related repo, was archived on 2025-06-06 and is a savedata Lua loader, not the claimed exploit. No Switch 1 package, offsets, or payload exist. Switch2Unlock labels the 2026-10-22 physical-cartridge and untethered claims 'Rumor / unconfirmed' and says none of it is released. Wccftech describes the untethered concept as a Switch 2 save-data installer providing userland-level access, not a Switch 1 package.
entries.limitations: Absence of public code at the time of checking does not prove no private work exists, and the author may release later. The 20.0.0+ figure is a Switch 2 compatibility requirement (E-048), not evidence about Switch 1 23.0.1. The exploit's target process and primitives are unknown, so its usefulness for reaching the fs sysmodule cannot be assessed.

entries.claim: CivSwitch 1.0 is a public MIT-licensed Switch 1 game-process exploit for Civilization VII 1.0.0 physical cartridge. A chat XSS runs JavaScript in the game's embedded V8 context, a pointer-compression exploit provides addrof/fakeobj and arbitrary read/write, and a ROP chain calls native game/SDK functions and exposes a TCP JavaScript loader on port 9026. It is stage 1 only: the public code contains no fs sysmodule payload or privilege escalation.
entries.scope: Read-only inspection of Gezine/CivSwitch release 1.0, README, core.js, PicoSwitch, and installer-creator on 2026-11-03. No code was run on a console.
entries.evidence: The repository was created 2026-10-28 and release 1.0 was published 2026-11-01. core.js (60,695 bytes) implements V8 pointer-compression primitives, addrof/fakeobj, arbitrary read/write, a ROP chain built from game main-image and SDK gadgets, call_rop, and nn::socket Socket/Bind/Listen/Accept/Connect/Recv/Send/Close wrappers. It starts a TCP listener on port 9026 and evaluates JavaScript received over it. The README describes the chain as an XSS toolchain for the Switch 1 edition of Civilization VII, with the Pico typing a chat payload and the Remote JS Loader running for that session. A repository tree and grep found no fs IPC calls, no fs sysmodule payload, and no privilege-escalation stage.
entries.limitations: The ROP offsets are for the Civ VII 1.0.0 game build; they do not establish system-firmware compatibility. Switch 1 23.0.1 is claimed but the README lists only Switch 1 22.5.0 as tested. The public code is a game-process primitive, not fs-level. No independent reproduction on a Switch 1 23.0.1 was found.

entries.claim: CivSwitch requires a paid Civilization VII 1.0.0 physical cartridge, a Pico RP2040/RP2350 USB HID (or equivalent typing macro), English(US) system and USB-keyboard settings, and a local-wireless lobby. The optional installer writes XSTRIG.Civ7Save and wipes save:/saves/Single/. Switch 1 23.0.1 is claimed but untested; Switch 1 22.5.0 is the only tested Switch 1 firmware.
entries.scope: README, PicoSwitch README, installer-creator README, and release 1.0 retrieved 2026-11-03. No purchase, install, or console test.
entries.evidence: The README says only the 1.0.0 version in physical cartridge is supported, every Switch 1/2 firmware from 20.x.x to 23.0.1 should work, and the tested configurations are Switch 1 22.5.0 and Switch 2 20.4.0/23.0.1. It requires English(US) system language and USB Keyboard language, a local-wireless host lobby, and the Pico typing about 87 chat lines over roughly 15-20 minutes. The installer README says it wipes every file in save:/saves/Single/, writes save:/saves/Single/XSTRIG.Civ7Save, and is optional for the session-only loader. GBAtemp reported the game was readily available in the UK for about £30 on 2026-11-01.
entries.limitations: The 23.0.1 Switch 1 configuration is claimed but not tested. The installer is destructive to Civ VII save data and is not needed for a first loader test. The Pico is an additional purchase. The game is paid, so the project's no-paid-games rule currently blocks the test.

entries.claim: Firmware 23.5.0 fixes the fs PathNormalizer::Normalize heap buffer overflow on Switch 1 and Switch 2, updates the anti-downgrade fuse list, and is required by dauth as of about 2026-11-16.
entries.scope: Public patch notes and wiki; 23.5.0 was not installed on the target.
entries.evidence: Switchbrew's 23.5.0 page lists the FS KIP as updated and records 'A vuln was fixed' for fs; its flaw table says the temporary path buffer is now sized to the source path up to 0x600 bytes. The same page says the anti-downgrade fuses were updated and that dauth required 23.5.0 as of about 2026-11-16. Atmosphère 1.12.2 and hekate 6.5.5 add 23.5.0 support, confirming the update is shared across the family.
entries.limitations: The wiki is community documentation; the fix details are consistent with the ns2jb write-up. The target remains on 23.0.1.

entries.claim: The Switch 1 fs sysmodule on 23.0.1 and below contains the PathNormalizer::Normalize overflow: a fixed 0x301-byte temporary buffer, source paths up to the 0x800-byte HIPC pointer buffer, and up to 0x4FF bytes of overflow, yielding arbitrary read/write including on Switch 2.
entries.scope: Public flaw documentation plus the ns2jb write-up; no local Switch 1 fs binary.
entries.evidence: The Switch System Flaws table entry says parent-directory replacement allocates a fixed 0x301-byte buffer and copies the source path without bounds checking; fs's PointerBufferSize is 0x800, so the overflow is up to 0x4FF bytes; 23.5.0 sizes the buffer to the source path up to 0x600. It labels the result 'fs-sysmodule heap buffer overflow. Allows arbitrary read/write including on [S2].' Pepsipu's write-up says the same sequence was tested on Switch 1.
entries.limitations: Confirms the bug class and the fix, not a packaged Switch 1 exploit. The exact Switch 1 23.0.1 fs offsets and heap layout remain unpublished.

entries.claim: The public Switch 2 fs chains (KaiHEN, Seedsow FS, CivSwitchFS, civ7-fs-kaihen) are Switch 2-only and do not provide a Switch 1 fs package.
entries.scope: Read-only repository review on 2026-11-25; no Switch 2 hardware and no execution.
entries.evidence: KaiHEN describes itself as a Switch 2 homebrew environment and minimal CFW with full NAND access. Seedsow FS drives kaiHEN on a retail Switch 2 23.0.1 from a Seedsow save and warns of brick risk. CivSwitchFS is tested only on Switch 2 23.0.1 with Civilization VII 1.0.0 and exposes a full fsp-srv handle; civ7-fs-kaihen targets Switch 2 23.0.1 and recommends CivSwitchFS-kaiHEN. None lists a Switch 1 build.
entries.limitations: Absence of a Switch 1 package in the reviewed repositories, not proof that no private port exists.

entries.claim: Atmosphère 1.12.2 and hekate 6.5.5 support 23.5.0; hekate 6.5.5 supersedes the earlier 6.5.4 ceiling at 23.0.1.
entries.scope: Firmware compatibility only.
entries.evidence: Atmosphère 1.12.2 adds basic support for 23.5.0; its fusee was re-released on 2026-11-13 to fix a nogc patch failure on 23.5.0. hekate 6.5.5 lists 'Latest HOS supported: 23.5.0' and a same-day fat32 NOGC fix.
entries.limitations: Firmware support does not create an entry point on Mariko.

entries.claim: The BigInt structured-clone desync WebKit exploit is tested only on Switch 2 20.4.0, is not verified on 23.0.1, succeeds about 5% of the time, and a failed attempt can kernel-panic with 2168-0002.
entries.scope: Author's README and source; no independent reproduction.
entries.evidence: The README states the target is the Switch 2 WifiWebAuthApplet, tested on 20.4.0, 'Has NOT been tested on 23.0.1 - needs porting, will not work', only works on about 5% of attempts, and an attempt that failed will crash with error code 2168-0002 (kernel panic). It lists UA AppleWebKit/613.0 NF/7.0.3.12.11 NintendoBrowser/5.2.0.55481, JIT disabled, WebGL/WASM disabled, and Gigacage disabled.
entries.limitations: Author claim only. The exploit is Switch 2-specific and includes PS5/x86_64-derived ROP, not a Switch 1 ARM64 chain.

entries.claim: The upstream WebKit safari-613-branch deserializer handles BigIntTag and BigIntObjectTag, so the public exploit's stated 'deserializer does not support the BigInt tag' premise does not match that upstream branch; Nintendo's Switch NetFront build may differ.
entries.scope: Source inspection of WebKit safari-613-branch; Nintendo's build is not available.
entries.evidence: In safari-613-branch's SerializedScriptValue.cpp, readTerminal has 'case BigIntTag: return readBigInt();' and 'case BigIntObjectTag: ... readBigInt ... BigIntObject::create'. The serializer's dumpIfTerminal writes BigIntTag for heap BigInts and BigIntObjectTag for boxed BigInts. The public exploit instead describes a serializer/deserializer pool-count divergence in Nintendo's webkit_3.12.11 build.
entries.limitations: Upstream 613 is not Nintendo's NetFront build; the Switch build could have a different clone implementation or a Nintendo-specific regression. No Switch 1 test has been run.

entries.claim: Independent project-zero-switch-mariko research confirms that the Mariko 23.0.1 WifiWebAuthApplet executes attacker pages with DOM, Fetch/XHR, and WebSocket but found no vulnerability or jailbreak.
entries.scope: Independent AI-assisted research report; one physical console test.
entries.evidence: The repository's Phase 12 record and report describe a physical test on 23.0.1: the applet returned its UA, executed DOM tests, completed Fetch/XHR with HTTP 200, and echoed a WebSocket message. The agent report says no public Mariko/23.0.1 browser-to-homebrew chain was found and that the highest lead is openWeb/BrowserDll, blocked on encrypted NCAs.
entries.limitations: Not peer-reviewed; the test confirms reachability, not exploitability.

entries.claim: The supernag is a persistent local state in system save 0x8000000000000049 and the setsys setting vulnerability!needs_update_vulnerability_policy; it blocks web applets and cannot be cleared by maintenance mode or system initialization on stock firmware.
entries.scope: CFW tool source plus community reports from 2018-2026; no stock API exposes it.
entries.evidence: Gag-Order mounts system save 0x8000000000000049, reads ns:vm NeedsUpdateVulnerability, and checks the setsys item 'vulnerability'/'needs_update_vulnerability_policy'; its patch flips NAGGED_BYTES to UNNAGGED_BYTES at ns_ssversion:/entry. switch-sys-tweak's FEAT_NSVM_SAFE mitms ns:vm to return 0 'to enable using web applets on outdated fws'. GBAtemp's 2019 PSA and the May 2026 captive-portal thread say the browser is blocked and that maintenance mode/system initialization do not clear it. A November 2026 r/switch2hacks post reports the same on 23.0.1 for SmileBASIC 4 and Civilization VII.
entries.limitations: The save/setting names and mechanism are from CFW tools and community reports; the exact event that set the flag on the target is not known.

entries.claim: The OLED's 2026-11-17 captive-portal attempt was blocked before the applet loaded, consistent with the local supernag rather than a network failure.
entries.scope: Local hardware observation.
entries.evidence: research/hardware-observations/webkit-portal-20261117T152521Z.local.jsonl shows only repeated 'NX NIFM/00' requests to '/', with no WifiWebAuthApplet page load. The owner reported that the console refused with a system-update message. The supernag mechanism explains why a served page would not open.
entries.limitations: The log alone cannot distinguish a supernag refusal from another applet-launch failure; the owner's screen observation and the known mechanism make the supernag explanation the best-supported one.

entries.claim: No stock-safe supernag clearance is known; the documented options are CFW patches, a NAND restore, or updating to at least the cached version, and updating to 23.5.0 would remove the fs vulnerability.
entries.scope: Historical community testing plus current CFW tooling and 23.5.0 patch notes.
entries.evidence: The 2019 PSA lists maintenance mode, console initialization, failed updates, and browser entry points as tested and ineffective, and says only CFW/Gag-Order or a NAND restore works; a later post says the only denag without updating to 8.1.0 was a cartridge update to the cached version. Gag-Order and switch-sys-tweak are CFW-only. 23.5.0 is the current cached version and patches fs.
entries.limitations: Community testing is historical (2018-2019) but the mechanism and reports are consistent through 2026. A future stock exploit could change this.

entries.claim: The luci-app-switch2-block OpenWrt plugin spoofs the Nintendo LAN test and blocks outbound traffic to prevent updates and supernag, but it does not open the browser or clear an existing supernag.
entries.scope: Project README; no router or console test.
entries.evidence: The README describes a standalone dnsmasq + uHTTPd that answers the Nintendo connection test with the expected header and firewall rules that block the console from the internet, 'to prevent updates/supernag'. It requires an OpenWrt router and the console's MAC.
entries.limitations: It is a prevention tool; the target console already has the flag. It also suppresses the captive-portal trigger.

entries.claim: Nintendo's November 2026 DMCA takedown removed 144 Picofly modchip-firmware repositories and other Switch projects; this does not change the software-only path.
entries.scope: News report; context only.
entries.evidence: TorrentFreak reported on 2026-11-11 that Nintendo's DMCA notice disabled 144 GitHub repositories of Picofly, SX Core, and HWFLY-related modchip firmware.
entries.limitations: No effect on the target's firmware or the public fs research.

entries.claim: The H-013 day-directory variant is prepared as two FAT32 images (benign and parent) with a 255-character crafted filename and a 777-byte path, but has not been written to a card or run.
entries.scope: Local image generation and read-only mount validation.

entries.claim: The 2026-11-12 supernag wave was reported on 23.0.1 for SmileBASIC 4 and Civilization VII after 23.5.0; the target's browser block is consistent with that wave.
entries.scope: Community report about Switch 2 titles plus the shared ns:vm mechanism.
entries.evidence: The r/switch2hacks announcement says multiple 23.0.1 users report supernag on SmileBASIC 4 and Civilization VII, that it forces an update to 23.5.0, and that maintenance mode does not clear it. Switchbrew says dauth began requiring 23.5.0 around 2026-11-16.
entries.limitations: The reports are about Switch 2 titles; the target is a Switch 1 OLED. The shared ns:vm mechanism and the local browser refusal make the same explanation likely, but the exact trigger is unproven.
